source: ConOps & OpsCon Evaluation Rules - AI-ready rules
purpose: classify documents as ConOps, OpsCon, Hybrid or Neither

fundamental_rules.name: Problem Space orientation
fundamental_rules.description: The document describes the current situation, stakeholder needs, environmental evolution, motivations for change and desired future outcomes. It does not explain how a future operational solution will operate.
evaluation_questions: Why is change needed?
Does the document focus on needs rather than realization?
fundamental_rules.purpose: The document describes the current situation, stakeholder needs, environmental evolution, motivations for change and desired future outcomes. It does not explain how a future operational solution will operate.

fundamental_rules.name: Solution Space orientation
fundamental_rules.description: The document describes how future services and capabilities will be operationally realized.
evaluation_questions: How are future operations performed?
Is a future operational SoS described?
fundamental_rules.purpose: The document describes how future services and capabilities will be operationally realized.

conops_rules.name: Current operational situation exists
conops_rules.description: The current operational world is described.
evaluation_questions: How is the mission performed today?
What operational limitations exist today?
conops_rules.purpose: The current operational world is described.

conops_rules.name: Stakeholders exist
conops_rules.description: Stakeholders affected by the problem are identified with role, interest and influence when available.
evaluation_questions: Who is affected?
Who benefits from future improvements?
conops_rules.purpose: Stakeholders affected by the problem are identified with role, interest and influence when available.

conops_rules.name: Operational environment exists
conops_rules.description: The operational or strategic environment is characterized.
evaluation_questions: What external factors influence the future concept?
Which environmental changes are expected?
conops_rules.purpose: The operational or strategic environment is characterized.

conops_rules.name: Motivation for change exists
conops_rules.description: The document explicitly justifies why change is needed.
evaluation_questions: Why is the current situation no longer satisfactory?
What happens if nothing changes?
conops_rules.purpose: The document explicitly justifies why change is needed.

conops_rules.name: Stakeholder needs and expected outcomes exist
conops_rules.description: Stakeholder needs, jobs-to-be-done, expected outcomes, desired improvements and pain points are described.
evaluation_questions: What does each stakeholder need to accomplish?
What outcomes do they expect?
conops_rules.purpose: Stakeholder needs, jobs-to-be-done, expected outcomes, desired improvements and pain points are described.

conops_rules.name: Future services exist
conops_rules.description: Future services expected by stakeholders are described from the user perspective and remain black-box.
evaluation_questions: Which services are expected in the future?
Which stakeholder needs does each service address?
conops_rules.purpose: Future services expected by stakeholders are described from the user perspective and remain black-box.

conops_rules.name: Capability gaps exist
conops_rules.description: High-level missing, insufficient or emerging capability needs are identified.
evaluation_questions: What capabilities are missing today?
Which capabilities are inadequate?
conops_rules.purpose: High-level missing, insufficient or emerging capability needs are identified.

conops_rules.name: Future capabilities exist
conops_rules.description: Future capabilities are solution-independent and may include roadmap intentions without detailed plans.
evaluation_questions: What capabilities must exist in the future operational world?
conops_rules.purpose: Future capabilities are solution-independent and may include roadmap intentions without detailed plans.

conops_rules.name: No committed operational architecture
conops_rules.description: A ConOps shall not commit to a future operational architecture or SoS structure.
evaluation_questions: Is the future solution already operationally designed?
Are architecture decisions committed?
conops_rules.purpose: A ConOps shall not commit to a future operational architecture or SoS structure.

conops_rules.name: No detailed operational realization
conops_rules.description: A ConOps shall not define executable realization of future services.
evaluation_questions: Is a scenario illustrative or executable?
Does it specify future operations?
conops_rules.purpose: A ConOps shall not define executable realization of future services.

conops_rules.name: Stakeholder-oriented future scenarios may exist
conops_rules.description: Illustrative future scenarios may clarify stakeholder experiences without becoming executable.
evaluation_questions: Does the scenario illustrate a future experience?
conops_rules.purpose: Illustrative future scenarios may clarify stakeholder experiences without becoming executable.

conops_rules.name: Shared future vision exists
conops_rules.description: The document establishes a shared understanding of the desired future operational world.
evaluation_questions: Can stakeholders visualize the future?
Does the document create common understanding?
conops_rules.purpose: The document establishes a shared understanding of the desired future operational world.

conops_rules.name: Constraints for future solutions exist
conops_rules.description: Constraints that any future OpsCon must respect are identified.
evaluation_questions: What must any future OpsCon respect?
What cannot change regardless of the solution?
conops_rules.purpose: Constraints that any future OpsCon must respect are identified.

conops_rules.name: Multiple opportunity areas may exist
conops_rules.description: The problem space may contain several opportunity areas and need not be exhaustive; multiple OpsCon responses may derive from one ConOps.
evaluation_questions: Does the ConOps leave room for multiple future responses?
conops_rules.purpose: The problem space may contain several opportunity areas and need not be exhaustive; multiple OpsCon responses may derive from one ConOps.

opscon_rules.name: Future Operational SoS exists
opscon_rules.description: The future operational System-of-Systems is explicitly identified.
evaluation_questions: What future operational SoS is being described?
opscon_rules.purpose: The future operational System-of-Systems is explicitly identified.

opscon_rules.name: SoS boundaries exist
opscon_rules.description: The boundaries of the future operational SoS are defined.
evaluation_questions: What belongs inside and outside the SoS?
opscon_rules.purpose: The boundaries of the future operational SoS are defined.

opscon_rules.name: Operational services are allocated
opscon_rules.description: Operational services are allocated to constituent systems with provider and beneficiary information.
evaluation_questions: Which constituent realizes each service?
Who provides and receives the service?
opscon_rules.purpose: Operational services are allocated to constituent systems with provider and beneficiary information.

opscon_rules.name: Operational scenarios exist
opscon_rules.description: Executable operational scenarios explain how the future SoS operates.
evaluation_questions: Can scenarios support architecture and requirement derivation?
opscon_rules.purpose: Executable operational scenarios explain how the future SoS operates.

opscon_rules.name: Operational flows exist
opscon_rules.description: Information, material, energy or financial flows among constituents are identified.
evaluation_questions: What is exchanged?
What triggers each exchange?
opscon_rules.purpose: Information, material, energy or financial flows among constituents are identified.

opscon_rules.name: Constituent systems are identified
opscon_rules.description: The constituent systems composing the future operational SoS are identified.
evaluation_questions: Which systems participate in operations?
What are their roles?
opscon_rules.purpose: The constituent systems composing the future operational SoS are identified.

opscon_rules.name: Promoter System of Interest is identified
opscon_rules.description: The System of Interest owned or developed by the Promoter is identified among constituents.
evaluation_questions: Which System of Interest belongs to the Promoter?
opscon_rules.purpose: The System of Interest owned or developed by the Promoter is identified among constituents.

opscon_rules.name: Capabilities are allocated
opscon_rules.description: Operational capabilities are allocated to constituents, including user-facing and lifecycle-facing capabilities when available.
evaluation_questions: Which constituent realizes each capability?
opscon_rules.purpose: Operational capabilities are allocated to constituents, including user-facing and lifecycle-facing capabilities when available.

opscon_rules.name: Interfaces supporting operational flows exist
opscon_rules.description: Technical, human-system or natural interfaces supporting operational flows are identified.
evaluation_questions: Which interfaces support exchanges?
What flow does each interface carry?
opscon_rules.purpose: Technical, human-system or natural interfaces supporting operational flows are identified.

opscon_rules.name: Operational context exists
opscon_rules.description: Future operational conditions, external systems and operating environment are described.
evaluation_questions: Under which conditions do operations occur?
opscon_rules.purpose: Future operational conditions, external systems and operating environment are described.

opscon_rules.name: Governance exists
opscon_rules.description: Authority, coordination, arbitration and resource allocation mechanisms are identified.
evaluation_questions: Who decides and coordinates?
Who resolves operational conflicts?
opscon_rules.purpose: Authority, coordination, arbitration and resource allocation mechanisms are identified.

opscon_rules.name: Operational dependencies exist
opscon_rules.description: Dependencies among services, systems and actors are described with criticality when available.
evaluation_questions: Which constituent depends on another?
What happens if the dependency fails?
opscon_rules.purpose: Dependencies among services, systems and actors are described with criticality when available.

opscon_rules.name: Traceability to originating ConOps exists
opscon_rules.description: Services, outcomes and constraints trace back to originating ConOps needs; value chain traceability may be explicit.
evaluation_questions: Which ConOps need does each service address?
Is traceability complete from need to service?
opscon_rules.purpose: Services, outcomes and constraints trace back to originating ConOps needs; value chain traceability may be explicit.

opscon_rules.name: Operational ownership exists
opscon_rules.description: Operational responsibilities and ownership are assigned; Promoter, Partner, Supplier or Alliance roles may be identified.
evaluation_questions: Who owns each operational responsibility?
opscon_rules.purpose: Operational responsibilities and ownership are assigned; Promoter, Partner, Supplier or Alliance roles may be identified.

opscon_rules.name: Operational modes exist
opscon_rules.description: Nominal, degraded, emergency or maintenance modes are described.
evaluation_questions: Which operational modes are defined?
opscon_rules.purpose: Nominal, degraded, emergency or maintenance modes are described.

classification_policy.conops_question: Why should the future operational world be different?
classification_policy.opscon_question: How will the future operational system-of-systems operate?
classification_policy.hybrid_rule: Both normalized family scores are at or above the high score threshold.
classification_policy.neither_rule: Both normalized family scores are below the minimum score threshold.
